item.title: Who are the Titans going to start at RG in Week 3?
item.description: The Tennessee Titans are dealing with two injuries at right guard ahead of their Week 4 matchup vs. the Ravens.
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans were hampered by the injury bug in their Week 3 loss to the New York Giants. Starting right guard Fernando Carmona quickly exited the defeat with an ankle injury. It’s since been reported by Jordan Schultz that Carmona will be sidelined on a week-to-week basis.

At least it’s not a season-ending injury for Carmona. The rookie right guard has been an early-season revelation. He was replaced by Jackson Slater, who performed serviceably.

The issue? Head coach Robert Saleh revealed Slater suffered a “significant” foot injury, but played through it. The working expectation is Slater will be sidelined even longer than Carmona will. The Titans placed them both on IR earlier this week.

So who do the Titans start at RG in Week 3 versus the Baltimore Ravens? OC Brian Daboll and OL Coach Carmen Bricillo have a few options to sort through. The straightforward option would be Atonio Mafi.

Mafi was added to the Titans’ 53-man roster just recently as a waivers claim. The fifth-round pick from UCLA in the 2023 NFL Draft has started just seven career games. He’s been below-average when afforded opportunities to play.

We’re not convinced Mafi will be the Titans’ choice. Garrett Dellinger was recently promoted to the active roster from the practice squad. Remember that Dellinger was the biggest surprise inclusion on the initial 53-man roster. He spent the entire offseason in this offense, and certainly knows the playbook better than Mafi does.

Dellinger actually played really well throughout the preseason. The former LSU product didn’t allow single a pressure or sack and scored PFF grades of 74.8, 72.3, and 80.3 in pass protection. His overall run-blocking grade was 81.9.

Is rookie Pat Coogan an alternative? He’s obviously far more comfortable at center than guard.

The Titans will probably start Dellinger or Mafi versus the Ravens. Would they consider reuniting with Kevin Zeitler? We’re excited to analyze whichever decision is made.

item.title: 3 bold reasons the Bengals will bounce back and beat the Jaguars
item.description: The Bengals should be ready for a rebound performance after their debacle in Pittsburgh.
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Bengals didn’t exactly get the result they wanted in Pittsburgh.

After opening the season 2-0, Cincinnati let a winnable game slip away from them in Week 3, falling 30-27 to the Steelers. Now, they get a chance to put that one behind them with the Jacksonville Jaguars coming to Paycor Stadium on Sunday.

And while Jacksonville is coming off a convincing 35-6 win over New England, there are plenty of reasons to believe the Bengals can get back in the win column.

Here are three bold reasons why.

1. Bengals’ response will be very different from performance in Pittsburgh

Let’s start with the obvious one: this team should be angry.

Cincinnati had a chance to walk out of Pittsburgh at 3-0 and instead came away with a divisional loss in which the Bengals made enough self-inflicted mistakes to cost themselves the game.

That’s the kind of loss that can either linger or serve as a wake-up call.

I’m betting on the latter.

The Bengals return home, where they’ll have a chance to correct those mistakes in front of their own fans. Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow have been around long enough to understand that one loss doesn’t define a season, but allowing the same mistakes to snowball would be a different story.

The Jaguars aren’t the Steelers. And Cincinnati should come out playing with the urgency of a team that doesn’t want to start a losing streak.

Bold prediction: Cincinnati scores first and never trails.

2. Jacksonville will struggle with Cincinnati’s passing game

The Jaguars’ defense has been opportunistic early this season, but this is where having Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins becomes a pretty significant advantage.

Through the first three games, Burrow has thrown for 461 yards and three touchdowns, while Higgins has 154 receiving yards and Chase has already established himself as the centerpiece of the offense. And don’t forget what happened the last time these teams played in Cincinnati.

The Bengals beat Jacksonville 31-27 in 2025, with Cincinnati’s passing game making several big plays late.

This matchup has the potential to become another one of those games where Jacksonville simply has too many weapons to account for.

The Jaguars can’t sell out to stop Chase because Higgins can hurt them. They can’t devote all of their attention to the receivers because Burrow is perfectly capable of picking apart favorable looks underneath.

And if the Bengals’ offensive line can give Burrow time? That’s where things could get really interesting.

Bold prediction: Chase goes over 100 receiving yards and finds the end zone.

3. Dexter Lawrence and defensive front will take over

Here’s the one I’m most interested in.

Cincinnati’s biggest offseason overhaul came up front, and the early returns have been encouraging. The Bengals entered Week 4 leading the NFL with eight sacks, according to the NFL’s game-center statistics.

Now they get to face a Jacksonville offense that has been productive but hasn’t exactly been unstoppable through the air.

The Jaguars are averaging 314 yards per game, while Cincinnati’s defense has already generated eight sacks and three takeaways through three games.

And this is where Dexter Lawrence can make his presence felt.

The Bengals brought Lawrence in to change the complexion of their defensive front. After recording two sacks against Aaron Rodgers in Pittsburgh, he now gets another opportunity to wreck an opposing quarterback’s afternoon.

If Cincinnati can generate pressure without constantly blitzing, it allows the secondary to play more aggressively and puts Jacksonville in some uncomfortable down-and-distance situations.

Bold prediction: Lawrence records another sack, while the Bengals finish with at least four as a team.

The Prediction

Look, this isn’t going to be a walk in the park. Jacksonville is coming off a 35-6 demolition of New England, and the Jaguars are 2-1 heading into Cincinnati.

But this feels like a classic “prove it” game for the Bengals.

And there is something about history. It tends to repeat itself.

If the Steelers win games against Cincinnati in the ways/scenarios we saw on Sunday, Lawrence and the Jags have an uphill battle. Since being drafted No. 1 overall by Jacksonville in 2021, Lawrence has not beaten the Bengals.

This includes a crazy Thursday Night affair in his rookie year, as well as a couple of other crazy Jake Browning games. On Monday Night Football in 2023, as well as in relief last year in Week 2, Browning led the Bengals to improbable wins in Burrow’s absence.

The Bengals have already shown they can win a close one. They showed they can dominate on the road against Houston. Now they need to show they can take a tough loss and respond.

The Bengals are back at Paycor Stadium. Burrow is healthy. Chase and Higgins give them matchup problems all over the field. And the revamped defensive front has already demonstrated that it can make life miserable for opposing quarterbacks.

So, let’s go bold:

Bengals 31, Jaguars 23.

A bounce-back win, a 3-1 record, and a much better feeling heading into the next stretch of the schedule.

item.title: Patriots opponent preview: Get to know the Bills
item.description: Players to watch, stats, injuries, and more for the Patriots’ opponent on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots are entering the fourth week of the 2026 NFL season off the worst defeat of the Mike Vrabel era, a 35-6 blowout at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Now at 1-2 and facing significant questions at quarterback and several other positions on and off the field, the team is in dire need of a rebound and some success to start righting the ship again.

Unfortunately, the next opportunity to do so will see the Patriots go up against one of the best teams in the NFL. The Buffalo Bills have won all three of their games so far and despite being led by a rookie head coach appear well-positioned to regain the AFC East crown they saw move to New England last season.

Ahead of the two rivals’ Week 4 meeting, let’s take a closer look at the Bills and what to expect from them on Sunday.

Bills key stats

When you start a season with three straight wins, you obviously are doing something right. In the Bills’ case it is playing offensive football. The unit led by former league MVP Josh Allen at quarterback has been one of the best in football no matter how you want to look at it.

Buffalo’s offense has been impressive so far this season, setting up a strength-versus-strength showdown with a Patriots defense that performed really well the first two weeks of the season before its worst outing in a while against the Jaguars last Sunday. New England will need to bring its A-game in order to slow down the Bills, especially in the run game: whereas the Patriots have been uneven defending the run, their upcoming opponent has been as good as any team in the league in that area.

As for Buffalo’s defense, it hasn’t performed on quite the same level. While still good enough to help the team start 3-0, it doesn’t stand out in any particular metric. For a Patriots offense all out of sorts so far this season, this is an opportunity to build some much-needed momentum.

Bills 2026 season

As noted above, the Bills started the year with three straight victories. The first one came on the road against Houston, followed by wins over the Lions and Chargers to move the team to 3-0 and the current second place in the AFC playoff picture.

Week 1: 36-31 win at Houston Texans (1-0)
Week 2: 41-31 win vs. Detroit Lions (2-0)
Week 3: 24-16 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers (3-0)

The Bills have certainly been impressive this year, but their opponents have all struggled as well. The Texans, Lions and Chargers are a combined 2-4 in their other games this year; both of those wins have come courtesy of the Lions.

As they have been for several years now, the Bills are all about Josh Allen. Possibly the best quarterback in the NFL, he is again off to a hot start.

In three games so far, Allen has completed 56 of 86 pass attempt (65.1%) for 786 yards with five touchdowns and two interceptions. In addition, he has gained 119 rushing yards and scored a league-leading six touchdowns on 23 non-kneel-down carries. Add his effective rushing performance — 5.2 yards per carry — to his passing success and you get a quarterback currently ranked fourth in the NFL in EPA per play (0.355). For comparison, his Patriots counterpart Drake Maye is ranked 28th (-0.070).

For as much of a cheat-code he can be, Allen cannot sustainably carry the Bills offense by himself. Luckily, his supporting cast has been top-notch as well, especially two players: running back James Cook, who has 346 rushing yards, two touchdowns, and a league-best 6.0 yards per carry to his name, and tight end Dalton Kincaid, catcher of a team-best 14 passes for 263 yards and a score.

Cook and Kincaid are two of the best players on an offense also heavily featuring the likes of D.J. Moore (11-167-1), Khalil Shakir (8-94-0) and Keon Coleman (8-101-0). Meanwhile, Joshua Palmer has scored on both of his receptions for a combined 77 yards.

The skill positions are complemented by a stout offensive line whose starters have all been with the team last year as well and who have played plenty of football together. That chemistry in combination with creative play designs and well-timed calls has allowed Buffalo to control the line of scrimmage in all three of its games thus far.

Defensively, Gregory Rousseau is the name to watch and somebody capable of giving the right side of the Patriots line all sort of problems. His six sacks are the most in the NFL so far this season, as are his three forced fumbles.

The Bills’ defensive line is a pick-your-poison unit up front, with Rousseau complemented by Bradley Chubb and a talented interior pairing in Ed Oliver and Deone Walker. If the top dog commands extra attention, the others are more than capable of winning 1-on-1s elsewhere.

Behind the talented front four, the Bills are again led by starting linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams; despite the team’s extensive coaching changes, the two have remained in place as the top two at the position.

Consistency in general has been a common theme for the Bills in multiple areas across their roster. One exception is the secondary, where two starters — safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson and nickel CB Dee Alford — only joined the team through free agency in March. Both have performed well this year, with Gardner-Johnson notching the team’s only interception so far. On the outside, Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston are a solid pairing.

Speaking of solid, Tyler Bass has gone 4-for-4 on field goals and 11-of-12 on extra points so far this year. Greg Dortch is averaging 9.0 yards per punt return.

Bills coaching staff

After suffering more playoff heartbreak with a divisional round exit in January, the Bills decided to fire head coach Sean McDermott after nine seasons and a combined record of 106-58. They eventually opted to promote offensive coordinator Joe Brady to the vacant position, and he surrounded himself with a competent staff: Pete Carmichael and Jim Leonhard were both poached from the Broncos, while veteran special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers was brought in to oversee the kicking game.

Also part of Brady’s staff are some names familiar to Patriots fans. Bo Hardegree, a one-time offensive assistant, is serving as quarterbacks coach, with former backup QB Trace McSorley an assistant on the offensive staff.
